correctness.rationale: For every nonempty face with at least two vertices, C4-freeness forces a unique common-neighbor center. For each center v and chosen r_v, descending-cardinality pairings (sigma,sigma union {r_v}) for sigma subset N(v)\{r_v}, |sigma|>=2 have unique remaining coface: every other larger coface was paired earlier and none belongs to a second center. The residue is exactly the union of rooted stars, with 2e-n distinct edges. Graph paths in the neighborhood one-skeleton are exactly even-length G-walks up to repetitions, so connected nonbipartite G gives a connected spine and rank 2e-2n+1. Independent code rebuilt all 3610 qualifying labeled n<=6 graphs, rechecked 7916 roots and 19974 elementary collapses; further exact face-replay tests checked large degree friendship graphs with and without a leaf. The finite tests corroborate, but do not prove, the universal statement; the proof is analytic. The arbitrary-root quantifier, triangles, pendant vertices and minimal n=3 were all considered.

evidence: The bipartite direct-collapse theorem covers every canonical bipartite double cover of the submitted graphs, so its domain dominates after a standard reduction.
The published high-girth neighborhood theorem 57f56ac6de4a uses the same descending-cardinality root pairings and already covers the minimum-degree-at-least-two, triangle-free subfamily.
The graph-like square-cycle theorem d8f86495e49d covers a different four-cycle-present family at the level of abstract homotopy, not the exact C4-free root-selection construction.
Kamibeppu 2008 Theorem 3 gives equivariant strong deformation retraction of the box complex to the double-cover graph in the C4-free case, but not this direct neighborhood simplicial-collapse model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The canonical cover H is connected because G has an odd closed walk; a 4-cycle in H would project to four distinct original vertices forming a 4-cycle in G. All earlier bipartite assumptions therefore hold, including possible triangles and degree-one vertices in G. Thus broad prior coverage fully subsumes the target after reduction. The high-girth theorem supplies an additional direct-overlap check, but the bipartite theorem is decisive.

value.rationale: The direct root-selected graph spine is a natural and useful structural object, but every mathematical assertion and its monotone collapse certificate is already delivered by the published square-free bipartite spine theorem after the routine canonical bipartite-double-cover substitution. The proposed nonbipartite presentation adds no independent structural lemma, new exact invariant, counterexample, boundary classification or non-implied classification. Its graph counts and wedge rank are immediate substitutions |V(H)|=2n, |E(H)|=2e. Thus correctness and the general utility of the inherited construction do not establish a distinct valuable research contribution.

limitations: The result is correct only for finite connected simple nonbipartite C4-free graphs, n>=3; no claim for C4-containing graphs.
